name: Aperture Finance arbitrary call approval drain
summary: The closed-source Aperture router forwarded caller-supplied call targets and calldata without validation, letting the attacker make the contract invoke ERC-20 transferFrom() and ERC-721 transfers against the standing token and Uniswap V3 position approvals users had granted it.
notes: The vulnerable arbitrary-call path is part of the target's immutable direct runtime, created by the factory in this transaction and unchanged through the exploit.

BlockSec reports approximately $3.67 million of gross assets lost across the Aperture campaign on Ethereum, Arbitrum, and Base. The structured asset component is the exact WBTC amount transferred from a victim in the selected Ethereum transaction; it is only one component of the reported cross-chain total. No recovery is netted from the exploit-time loss.
The cross-chain $3.67 million campaign total is retained from BlockSec reporting; only the selected Ethereum transaction's WBTC component was independently quantified here.
